findings.body:
**Add the required report version to the fixture.**

`test/ops/review/addressManyPlan.test.ts:84` returns an object without `version`. `ReviewAddressReport` requires `version: 1` (`src/ops/review/address.ts:147–251`). The final `Partial<ReviewAddressReport>` spread does not guarantee that field, so typechecking this file fails.

Add `version: 1` to the default report object.
findings.title: Add the required report version to the fixture.

findings.body:
**Pass `target: 'merge-queue'` to the runner in this fixture.**

`run()` calls `makeReviewRun(deps)` without `target`. The runner resolves a missing target to `main`, but the fixture enrolls `merge-queue` debt. The runner's binding match compares `binding.target` with that resolved target. The run can therefore fail to find the seeded enrollment, and the settlement assertions may not exercise the path they are meant to test. Set the target explicitly so the run uses the same target as the seeded debt.

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
-    run: () => makeReviewRun(deps)({ repoRoot: repo.root }),
+    run: () => makeReviewRun(deps)({ repoRoot: repo.root, target: 'merge-queue' }),
```

</details>
findings.title: Pass `target: 'merge-queue'` to the runner in this fixture.

findings.body:
**Give the managed-route test a `managedSubmit` fixture and assert managed submission.**

Without `managedSubmit`, the CodeRabbit leg does not launch the CLI. It returns needs-human instead. The scripted `coderabbit` response at lines 52-55 is never used, so the vendor source cannot become `terminal`. The assertions at lines 285 and 292-294, and the single `coderabbit` call expected at line 295, cannot hold.

Pass a successful managed submit in the run dependencies, as the sibling changed-head tests do (`managedSubmit: managedTerminal([])` in `test/ops/review/settledPredecessorFindings.freshChangedHead.test.ts:42`). Replace the line 295 CLI-call assertion with an assertion that `managedSubmit` was called once. Remove the `coderabbit` stub at lines 52-55.

findings.body:
**Set the fixture origin target to `merge-queue`.**

`cycleRecord` defaults `target` to `main`. The origin at `test/ops/review/finalRefreshBookkeeping.test.ts:127-136` keeps that default. When `prepareDeferredVendorReview` runs for `merge-queue` at line 137 without a retained `merge-queue` lineage, the fresh-origin branch in `src/ops/dev/internal/deferredLedger.ts` checks `vendor.target !== target` at line 428. A mismatch returns `undefined` at line 430. The fixture then throws `missing genuine persisted debt` at line 138, so setup fails before the settlement assertions run. The check at lines 480-481 is not the rejecting check on this path.

Setting `target: 'merge-queue'` on the origin makes the fresh-origin check pass. The origin then carries the requested target through the later check at line 480.

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
 // test/ops/review/finalRefreshBookkeeping.test.ts
   const origin = cycleRecord({
     cycleId: 'genuine-outage',
+    target: 'merge-queue',
     head: state.head,
```

</details>
findings.title: Set the fixture origin target to `merge-queue`.
